questions.q: Glucose on prolonged heating with HI gives n-hexane. This shows that:
options: glucose exists as a cyclic hemiacetal
the six carbon atoms of glucose form an unbranched chain
questions.explain: HI removes all the oxygen without changing the carbon skeleton, and the product is the straight-chain alkane, so the carbons of glucose are in a straight chain.

questions.q: What is the role of red phosphorus in the HI/red P reducing system?
options: It converts the I₂ formed back into HI via PI₃, so it is the reductant actually used up
It acts as a Lewis acid catalyst that activates C–O bonds
It absorbs the water formed during the reduction
It reduces the substrate directly, without HI taking part
questions.explain: HI is oxidised to I₂ as it reduces the substrate; red P forms PI₃, which water hydrolyses to H₃PO₃ and HI, so only a small amount of HI is needed.

questions.q: Which reagent reduces an aldehyde or ketone only as far as the alcohol, unlike HI/red P?
options: Prolonged heating with conc. HI/red P
questions.explain: Hydride reagents such as NaBH₄ stop at the alcohol, whereas HI/red P also removes the OH group. Clemmensen and Wolff–Kishner both convert C=O to CH₂.

questions.q: Under mild two-phase conditions (toluene–water, HI/red P), which compound is reduced to the hydrocarbon most readily?
questions.explain: Benzylic alcohols are reduced easily; under mild conditions non-benzylic alcohols stop at the alkyl iodide, and ester and keto groups survive. Complete reduction to the alkane needs prolonged heating with concentrated HI.
